questions.prompt: Which listed subtopic is explicitly part of “Component-Based Refactoring”?
options: Defining clear component inputs and outputs
questions.explanation: The supplied curriculum lists “Replacing controller-heavy views with components” under Component-Based Refactoring. Review that subtopic in the lesson and map it to the actual version-specific behavior.

questions.prompt: What is the safest way to apply component-based refactoring in a legacy application?
options: Confirm the deployed AngularJS version, keep responsibilities clear, and test observable behavior including a relevant edge case.
Assume the sample can be pasted into production without checking module or dependency versions.
Move authorization and validation entirely into the frontend.
Skip tests when the template appears to render correctly.
questions.answer_key: Confirm the deployed AngularJS version, keep responsibilities clear, and test observable behavior including a relevant edge case.
questions.explanation: Legacy maintenance requires version awareness, explicit ownership and repeatable checks; a rendered happy path does not demonstrate security or error-path correctness.

questions.prompt: Which evidence best supports a change related to component-based refactoring?
options: A repeatable check for normal behavior plus a relevant boundary/error/cleanup case, with expected results documented.
A screenshot with no record of the input or environment.
A course streak or activity count.
A passing static parse with no behavioral verification.
questions.answer_key: A repeatable check for normal behavior plus a relevant boundary/error/cleanup case, with expected results documented.
questions.explanation: Observable repeatable checks make legacy changes safer and provide a basis for regression tests.
